source.display_title: 05/12/2026 - Bryan Langsdale x Harry Edmonds  — Follow Up

prospect.name: Bryan Langsdale
prospect.location: Northern Washington State, near the Canadian border, USA
prospect.family_status: Has a girlfriend, from Vancouver, Canada
prospect.training_background: Former yoga teacher of several years; ~7-8 years of barbell/bodybuilding-style gym training which he abandoned; started kettlebells ~4 months ago, cancelled his gym membership and bought a full home set (15, 25, 35, 50, 60 and 100 lb). Trains 4-5 days a week: pull day, posterior chain day, push day, plus flow days with windmills, cleans and clean presses, macebells, sandbags, rings and beach carries. Self-reports losing ~30 lb over the past 18 months.
prospect.medical: Reports historic back problems and joint pain from his barbell/bodybuilding era, which he says resolved after switching to kettlebells. Currently smashing his wrists on cleans and snatches, a concern because he works with his hands as a massage therapist. No current diagnosis, medication or treatment disclosed.

signals: Self-directed and already getting results without coaching: 'it actually has been melting off slowly for a while... I probably melted 30 pounds off in the past year and a half'
Declined the coaching price on the spot without negotiating: 'honestly, the 4K, I'm not going to go for that right now. I'm just going to tell you straight.'
Anchored to the low-cost self-guided tier: '200 a month seems pretty legit, and it seems like there's a lot of stuff there'
Actively comparison shopping: 'I'm checking out a couple other programs, and you're like the second one I've looked at'
Not a rebuilder or optimizer archetype in the classic sense — he is buying critique, not transformation

goals.text: Get his kettlebell technique properly critiqued, especially cleans and snatches, so he stops smashing his wrists
Structure and progress his own flows properly instead of guessing when to move up in bell weight
Melt off the remaining layer of belly and chest fat over his existing muscle
Train for the long run without destroying his joints — longevity and function into his 80s, modelled on his own 80-year-old clients who still ski and climb

pains.text: Banging his wrists on cleans and snatches with the 50 lb bell; he is a massage therapist and needs to protect his hands
Cannot self-correct form from online videos — 'that's not the same as having somebody that can be like, yo, do this'
Barbell training was destroying his joints and giving him back problems
Stubborn subcutaneous fat remaining despite a clean carnivore-leaning diet; suspects he over-eats fat, does not track macros ('yeah, I just downed like 3,800 calories')
Risk of letting ego push him to a heavier bell before he has earned it — 'I got into trouble with that and with barbells'
Years of unresolved trauma previously kept him from accomplishing his goals

objections.raw_quote: Because honestly, the 4K, I'm not going to go for that right now. I'm just going to tell you straight.
objections.rep_response: Did not isolate the objection or explore finances at all. Immediately accepted it and screen-shared the $200/month self-guided product instead.

objections.raw_quote: I am looking for something a little more catered to me with the things I'm doing, like, I'm not looking for my hand to be held, but I'm really looking for the critique, and I can understand it, like, okay, for three months at a 4K, that'd probably be to, like, okay, I'm going to sit down with you and, like, do every little thing.
objections.rep_response: Explained the coaching includes 24/7 support from Trevor and full tailoring, framed it as 'hiring a mentor rather than a personal trainer', then introduced further reduced tiers: six months for 6K and one month for 1,200.

objections.raw_quote: Cool. Yeah, I got a bit to think about. I'm going to be honest, I'm checking out a couple other programs, and you're like the second one I've looked at here and trying to see what really fits.
objections.rep_response: Agreed and let it go — 'Yeah, cool, man. Well, just let me know.' No attempt to run the think-about-it play.

objections.raw_quote: I got trainers and kind of courses to go through, and once I do all four of them, I'll make a decision.
objections.rep_response: No differentiation attempted against the other four options he is evaluating.

evidence: Prospect explicitly declined the coaching price live: 'honestly, the 4K, I'm not going to go for that right now'
Ended undecided and comparison shopping: 'I just need some time to really make a decision'
Prospect took ownership of the next contact: 'I'll shoot you a text over on my word number, and you can get back to me when you're ready'
Counter-evidence of interest: prospect was warm on the self-guided tier ('200 a month seems pretty legit') and asked practical product questions about mobile optimisation at the end
No payment taken, no payment link sent, no next call booked
outcome.next_step: Prospect to text the rep after evaluating three other programmes; no date set and no follow-up call booked by the rep.

notable.note: The rep quoted an entire price ladder that does not exist in the sanctioned offer — 1 month $1,200, 3 months $4,000, 6 months $6,000, plus a $200/month self-guided product — and volunteered the cheapest option himself before any close attempt. He also stated an unlimited upgrade-credit policy ('It's just the difference every time') that should be checked against company position. The call never ran a consequence frame or a commitment check; it functioned as a product demo rather than a sales call.

quality.notes: Frequent block-level attribution swaps. Whole rep turns are labelled 'Bryan' and vice versa — e.g. the discovery question 'What was it that you were hoping we could potentially help you out with, man?' is labelled Bryan, and the prospect's answer about Sedona and the Washington location is split across both labels. The screen-share walkthrough passage at 00:20:08 onward is attributed to Bryan but is plainly the rep. Roles were resolved from content throughout.
